column1: DOMAIN GENERALIZATION — Expanded Lexicon Benchmark Results

Tests proving the engine is function-first and domain-agnostic. Same lexicons, same gates, same coordinate logic applied across SEC filings, journalism, healthcare, defense, academia, and political speech. Source: EE_Comprehensive_Lexicon_Rebuild_v1.xlsx → Summary sheet (rows 20–25).

column2: Engine correctly classifies 5/6 as CLEAN and 1/6 as EVASION (political polemic). No false positives on factual domains (healthcare, defense, academia).

Coordinate placement varies by content, not domain. Clinical trial (HEAD+STABILITY, Y=+0.37) behaves like an SEC filing, not like the political polemic (HEART−, Y=−0.23). The lexicons are measuring rhetorical function, not subject matter.
Bureaucratic_masking and scientism fire on institutional texts (SEC + Reuters) but not on healthcare, defense, or academic texts — correctly distinguishing laundering from technical register.

Political polemic correctly triggers EVASION gate (evasion_count threshold met). Coordinate Y=−0.23 reflects heart-lean from 'fight back', 'enemy', 'existential'. Testability = immunizing (unfalsifiable claims).

Expanded lexicon produces X/Y values in the 0.2–0.9 range — larger than GPT o3 (~0.00–0.15) but smaller than Gemini (0.8–5.0). Expanded lexicons close roughly 50% of the Gemini–GPT o3 compression gap.
